description: Generate a slide-deck-quality Stop Start Continue chart: three equal columns, Stop (red, a stop-sign marker), Start (emerald, a play marker) and Continue (sky, a circular-arrow marker), each a softly tinted panel with up to 8 bullets, plus an optional subject ("Sprint 14 retro") and an optional conclusion band for the agreed actions. Set `order: "start-stop-continue"` when the user puts Start first; rename columns with `labels` (e.g. { "continue": "Keep doing" }). Choose it for sprint and project retrospectives, team or manager feedback, and reviews of a process, project or habit; use create_swot for a strategic assessment of a company or product, a Harvey ball matrix to score options against criteria, and a mind map for an open-ended brainstorm. All three lists are optional, but fill all three; infer 3–5 bullets each from context rather than asking. Limits: 8 bullets per column of about 3–8 words, column names of 1–3 words, a conclusion of one sentence. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

inputSchema.description: A Stop Start Continue chart: three equal columns of up to 8 bullets each, what to stop doing, what to start doing and what to keep doing, with an optional subject line and conclusion. Used for retrospectives, feedback and project reviews.

examples.conclusion: Actions: review rule in the repo by Friday; protect sprint scope
examples.subject: Payments team
examples.title: Sprint 14 retrospective

colors.description: Optional colour overrides per column, as hex, e.g. { "stop": "#b91c1c" }. Each colours that column's stripe, marker, bullet dots and tint. Default: red, emerald and sky (or the brand palette).

conclusion.description: Optional one-line takeaway or list of agreed actions shown in a muted band under the columns, e.g. "Actions: Sam sets up review rules by Friday; Priya books the support demo". Wraps to 2 lines. Omit for none.

continue.description: What to keep doing: what works and should carry on, e.g. ["Daily stand-up at 9:30", "Blameless incident reviews"]. 0–8 short phrases. Always the last column. Default [].

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

labels.description: Optional column names in place of the standard Stop, Start and Continue, e.g. { "continue": "Keep doing" }. An empty or missing name shows the standard one. Up to 30 characters; 1–3 words read best.

continue.description: Name of the Continue column, e.g. "Keep doing". Default "Continue".

start.description: Name of the Start column, e.g. "Start doing". Default "Start".

stop.description: Name of the Stop column, e.g. "Stop doing". Default "Stop".

look.description: Drawing style, the same in every tool. "regular": clean lines and Inter (the default). "bold": heavier, slightly larger type and thicker lines, for slides read from a distance. "sketch": hand-drawn, with a handwriting font and pen lines that wobble a little, for early ideas and workshops. Use the one the user asks for; otherwise leave it out.

order.description: Column order: "stop-start-continue" (default) or "start-stop-continue". Continue is always last. Match the order the user writes.

palette.description: Hex colours. With the default palette the columns are red (Stop), emerald (Start) and sky (Continue); pass brand colours and they apply to the columns left to right instead. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

start.description: What to start doing: new practices worth trying, e.g. ["Pair on risky stories", "Demo to support every sprint"]. 0–8 short phrases. Default [].

stop.description: What to stop doing: habits or practices that waste time or hurt results, e.g. ["Merging without code review", "Status meetings with no agenda"]. 0–8 short phrases of about 3–8 words; long ones wrap to 3 lines. Default [].

subject.description: Optional subject of the review, e.g. "Sprint 14 retro" or "Q3 onboarding review", shown small and muted in the title row's right corner (or above the columns when the title is long). Omit for none.

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400, default 1280, which suits a 16:9 slide). PNG output renders at 2x. Height is computed from the content.
